column1: # The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time (Nintendo Switch 2 Edition; NVN2, Ampere shaders) on Android: an untested first profile written with the nxnative upsync of 2026-11-08
# (upstream to 7f5022200). Rows are those of the other Switch 2 profiles (Donkey Kong Bananza, Welcome Tour) whose reason holds for any Switch 2 game on the Odin 3; nothing here is
# tuned for this game yet. Upstream's Ocarina fixes that reach Android: the frame step stubs (patches.py, MATCH_FRAME_STEP), the dynamic-resolution stub (DM_DYNAMIC_RESOLUTION),
# raw 128-bit global loads as one vector load (translator), the colour write mask from the pixel shader's output map (gfx_vk_exec.c, needs a rebuilt shader bundle),
# timestamp reports known until they land for its conditional rendering (render_cond on in game.tsv)
status
package
orientation
# Handheld mode: on the Odin's 1080p screen the game targets its handheld resolution instead of the docked one (as Bananza and Welcome Tour)
setting
setting
setting
# The replay on its own thread (as Bananza)
env
# The host's adaptive frame rate off, as the other Switch 2 profiles. Proposal to check: with upstream's frame step stubs this game's step is the host's, so a 40 fps step may run at
# the right speed here, unlike Bananza
env
# DM_VK_PART_PACE: the backend default (on)
# Proposals for an A/B on the device, not set:
#   env DM_DYNAMIC_RESOLUTION=1   the game's dynamic resolution through upstream's climbing stub (0, the default, holds 1536x864)
#   env DM_VK_RC_QUEUE=1          render-enable state kept per NVN queue across submissions, as upstream's logical queues do (the queue-ordering fix for its flashes is Apple-only)
#   env DM_GPU_MIN_FREQ=967000000 the GPU clock floor the other Switch 2 profiles use (through su)
# Movies (2026-11-08, Odin 3): the AV1 movies decode on MediaCodec (c2.qti.av1.decoder; the game reads the pictures on the CPU, so they go through NV12 copies into its linear
# textures). The NDVE enhancement network the game runs over each decoded picture (Movie/Ndve/Ndve-Nvn2-vid_seq5.dat.zs, 22 compute shaders of 0.15-1.8 MB of SPIR-V with up to
# 1,000 subgroup shuffles) does not build on Adreno 830's driver: vkCreateComputePipelines fails on e6be82d835fbe4d3 and throws std::bad_alloc on d15370a382630d4e, which ends the app.
# Its stages are left out. The final title output instead receives the decoded picture through the tested movie-fill path below; enhancement is not reproduced.
env
env
# Device capture identifies 4f41 as the title background producer: its UNORM storage view covers a native SRGB image. The host converts a synchronized NV12 snapshot,
# scales in UNORM, and copies the encoded bytes into that image. Confirmed animated title background on Odin3; later cutscene outputs remain unverified.
# Only the observed final producer is filled; this key must also be in DM_VK_PASSTHRU_CS.
env
